title: Provision the SANDBOXES container binding so a run can actually boot
description:
BLOCKS THE EPIC ACCEPTANCE. Phase 1s definition of done is "a pushed epic submitted with tk cloud run completes end to end in one cloud orchestrator sandbox". That cannot happen today:

  live /health bindings: run_rooms, artifacts, db, run_workflow — NO sandboxes
  cloud/factory/wrangler.toml: no [[containers]] block, no SANDBOXES binding
  run-workflow.ts acquireContext: refuses when sandboxBinding(env) === null

Everything else is built, deployed and correct — the lease, the run API, the Workflow, gateway routing, artifact streaming, the operator channel, the image itself (3q2) and the entrypoint (orl). The one missing link is that nothing DECLARES the container binding or PUSHES the image to Cloudflare, so the control plane will refuse every run with "the SANDBOXES binding is not configured on this deployment".

The refusal message even says "re-run tk factory deploy" — but deploy cannot fix it, because the declaration does not exist in the bundle. That is the tell: a correct error pointing at a remedy that does nothing.

Work:
1. Declare the container/sandbox binding in cloud/factory/wrangler.toml against the image 3q2 builds, with the Durable Object class the SDK requires and its migration.
2. Teach tk factory deploy to build and push that image to the operator account registry before deploying the Worker, and to fail with an actionable error when the image is missing rather than deploying a Worker that refuses every run.
3. Verify LIVE: /health reports the sandboxes binding, and a submitted run boots one container and reaches the skill loop. Nothing short of a real boot closes this — a green test would repeat exactly the mistake this epic keeps catching.

Note the platform floor: containers/sandboxes may need a plan tier or an account flag beyond the Workers paid plan. If provisioning is blocked on an account setting, report that as a BLOCKED status naming the setting rather than working around it.

closed_reason: Completed: the SANDBOXES container binding is declared, the image is built and pushed by tk factory deploy (failing actionably when it cannot), and a real container boots and streams output through the adapter — proven live, with /health reporting sandboxes: true.
